paragraphs: The paper studies how to give formal meaning to alignment when an autonomous agent makes decisions affecting society. Its starting concern is that an agent's ability to process complex information does not establish that its objectives serve the people affected. The authors draw on utility theory and social choice theory to define alignment quantitatively in this setting.

Using that definition, they introduce policies that are probably approximately aligned: policies whose decisions are near optimal in the formal sense developed by the paper. They derive a sufficient condition for such policies to exist. This establishes one route to an existence guarantee; it does not make that condition necessary or show that practical agents automatically satisfy it.

Because meeting the condition is difficult in practice, the authors also consider a weaker target: policies that are safe in the sense of being nondestructive. They propose a safeguard for an agent's black-box policy that verifies the safety of its actions within their framework. The contribution therefore distinguishes achieving near-optimal social decisions from preventing destructive ones.
neurips-2024-can-an-ai-agent-safely-run-.tldr: The paper defines social alignment mathematically, gives a sufficient condition for near-optimal policies to exist, and proposes a safeguard for nondestructive actions.

paragraphs: Neural ordinary differential equations describe how a learned system evolves continuously through time. The paper argues that compact versions of these models can be too restrictive for physical dynamics that require a more flexible formulation. Increasing flexibility, however, introduces complicated nonlinear behavior, making it harder to establish how the modeled system will behave over time.

ControlSynth Neural ODEs address this tension by combining a more general model with convergence conditions expressed as tractable linear inequalities. These conditions provide a manageable way to guarantee convergence despite the model's nonlinear structure. The authors also add a control term intended to help learn dynamics at multiple scales simultaneously, a capability they identify as potentially useful for systems formulated using partial differential equations.

The experiments compare CSODEs with representative neural networks on physical dynamics suited to the model's inductive biases. In those settings, CSODEs show better learning and prediction. The stated result connects mathematical control over convergence with empirical modeling benefits, while keeping the predictive advantage tied to the physical settings evaluated.
neurips-2024-controlsynth-neural-odes-mo.tldr: CSODEs combine flexible continuous-time dynamics with tractable convergence conditions and show improved prediction on physical systems suited to their design.

paragraphs: Dash cameras record driving scenes across many vehicles and environments, making their videos an appealing source for reconstructing scenes and rendering new viewpoints. A major obstacle is the windshield: reflections and occlusions can obscure the outside world. The paper addresses these effects directly instead of treating dash-camera footage as equivalent to the video typically collected by autonomous vehicles.

DC-Gaussian builds on 3D Gaussian Splatting and introduces an adaptive image decomposition module that models reflections and occlusions together. An illumination-aware component accounts for how these obstructions change under different lighting conditions. A further enhancement uses geometric guidance to improve the details represented by the Gaussians. These components address both unwanted image content and the quality of the underlying scene reconstruction.

Experiments use both self-captured and public dash-camera videos. The authors report state-of-the-art novel-view synthesis performance and accurate reconstructions with obstructions removed. The stated findings support adapting neural rendering to the specific visual interference in windshield footage, helping make this widely available video source useful for scene reconstruction.
neurips-2024-dc-gaussian-improving-3d-ga.tldr: DC-Gaussian models windshield interference and lighting changes to improve scene reconstruction and novel-view rendering from dash-camera videos.

paragraphs: Models trained on biased data can learn spurious correlations that work during training but undermine generalization. DeNetDM approaches this problem through network depth. The authors establish theoretical results connecting examples that exhibit spurious correlations to a lower-rank manifold, and connecting network depth to implicit regularization of the rank of attribute representations.

These results motivate a training scheme with deep and shallow branches that develop biased and debiased representations. The branches are trained using a paradigm derived from Product of Experts, and their learned knowledge is then distilled into the target debiased model. Depth therefore becomes an active part of the debiasing mechanism, rather than simply a choice about the model's size or capacity.

The method requires neither annotations identifying the bias nor explicit data augmentation. The authors report performance competitive with approaches that need one or both, alongside a reported 5% improvement over existing debiasing techniques on synthetic and real-world datasets. The findings suggest that architectural differences can provide useful structure for learning robustness to spurious correlations without directly labeling those correlations.
neurips-2024-denetdm-debiasing-by-networ.tldr: DeNetDM uses network depth to separate biased and debiased learning, improving robustness without bias annotations or explicit data augmentation.

paragraphs: Automatic prompt optimization often starts with a collection of candidate prompts and then chooses one. The paper focuses on the cost of that choice: testing candidates requires model calls and evaluation of their responses. A strong candidate-generation method alone does not determine how efficiently a limited evaluation budget is spent.

TRIPLE treats prompt selection as fixed-budget best-arm identification, a problem from multi-armed bandits. In this connection, candidate prompts correspond to alternatives whose performance must be assessed before the budget runs out. The framework draws on methods developed for that problem while incorporating characteristics specific to prompt optimization. This makes the spending limit an explicit part of selection rather than an incidental practical concern.

Experiments across multiple tasks and language models show improved performance over baselines while respecting the imposed budgets. The authors also extend TRIPLE to selecting examples for few-shot prompts, with favorable empirical results. The contribution is therefore an approach to making better selection decisions with limited evaluations, covering both prompt candidates and the examples included in prompts.
neurips-2024-efficient-prompt-optimizati.tldr: TRIPLE uses fixed-budget best-arm identification to select effective prompts and few-shot examples while explicitly limiting evaluation costs.

paragraphs: Statistical independence tests ask whether two variables are related. This paper examines tests based on the Hilbert-Schmidt Independence Criterion, or HSIC, through a frequency-domain interpretation. The analysis identifies a source of limited detection power: an inflexible configuration cannot adapt to frequency features that are especially informative about the dependence present in the data.

The proposed method introduces learnable Fourier features and builds a new testing criterion around them. The authors model the criterion's behavior to estimate test power from a finite sample, then use that estimate as the objective for learning significant feature pairs. The objective can be computed in time linear in the sample count, supporting efficient optimization as datasets grow.

The paper also proves convergence of the optimization objective and consistency of the resulting independence tests. Experiments on synthetic and real data show advantages in both effectiveness and efficiency, particularly for high-dimensional and large-scale problems. Together, these results connect adaptation to informative frequency structure with computational efficiency and theoretical support for the testing procedure.
neurips-2024-efficiently-learning-signif.tldr: The method learns informative Fourier feature pairs to improve independence-test power using an objective whose computation scales linearly with sample size.

paragraphs: Dataset condensation creates a small synthetic dataset intended to preserve useful information from a much larger original dataset. Its appeal is more efficient model training while retaining diversity and realism in the synthetic examples. The paper identifies two obstacles in earlier approaches: expensive computation that restricts scaling, and design choices that leave potential improvements unexplored.

Elucidate Dataset Condensation, or EDC, addresses these obstacles through a framework centered on the design of the condensation process. Its strategies include soft category-aware matching, changes to the learning-rate schedule, and small training batches. The authors support these choices with both empirical evidence and theory, bringing several decisions together into an approach evaluated at small and large dataset scales.

For ImageNet-1k, the authors report 48.6% accuracy with ResNet-18 using ten synthetic images per class, corresponding to a compression ratio of 0.78%. They report that this outperforms the compared condensation methods. The finding shows how a carefully designed condensation process can retain substantial training value in a very small synthetic dataset under the tested configuration.
neurips-2024-elucidating-the-design-spac.tldr: EDC improves dataset condensation through coordinated matching and training choices, reporting strong accuracy with heavily compressed synthetic datasets.

paragraphs: Kernel k-means groups data using similarities represented by a kernel. The paper addresses a concern that conventional versions can overlook: a partition may be useful for clustering while also raising fairness issues. The authors incorporate fairness directly into the clustering framework so that it becomes part of the optimization process.

Their Fair Kernel K-Means method adds a fairness regularization term designed to have a form similar to the underlying clustering objective. This compatibility allows the term to be integrated into kernel k-means. The authors then extend the approach to a setting with multiple kernels, yielding Fair Multiple Kernel K-Means and carrying the fairness mechanism into a broader similarity representation.

The paper provides theoretical analysis of a generalization-error bound and uses it to derive a strategy for setting the hyperparameter. That connects a practical configuration choice to the theoretical analysis. Experiments in both single-kernel and multiple-kernel settings compare the proposed approaches with state-of-the-art methods and demonstrate their effectiveness. The contribution combines a fairness-aware objective, an extension across kernel settings, and guidance for configuring the method.
neurips-2024-fair-kernel-k-means-from-si.tldr: The paper integrates a fairness regularizer into single-kernel and multiple-kernel k-means and derives guidance for setting its hyperparameter.

paragraphs: The paper considers goal-oriented decision problems in which the relevant goal depends on context, using data that has already been collected. Its method, Contextual goal-Oriented Data Augmentation, or CODA, starts from unlabeled trajectories together with context-goal pairs. The central task is to turn these available information sources into data suitable for learning contextual decisions.

CODA constructs an action-augmented Markov decision process that is equivalent to the original decision process. Through this construction, it produces a fully labeled transition dataset for the training contexts without introducing additional approximation error. The equivalence matters because the data transformation is supported by a relationship to the original problem, rather than merely producing labels for a different decision task.

The authors provide a theoretical analysis of CODA's ability to solve these problems in an offline setting. Experiments also show that it outperforms baseline methods across different relationships between contexts and goals. The stated contribution is a principled way to make unlabeled trajectories useful for contextual goal-oriented learning, supported by both an error-preserving construction and empirical comparisons.
neurips-2024-how-to-solve-contextual-goa.tldr: CODA transforms unlabeled trajectories and context-goal pairs into labeled offline training data through an equivalent action-augmented decision process.

paragraphs: Creating a realistic avatar from one color image is difficult when clothing is loose or objects obscure parts of the person. Pretrained 2D diffusion models provide useful shape information, but the views they generate do not inherently come with guaranteed 3D consistency. Human-3Diffusion addresses this by coupling multi-view image generation with explicit 3D reconstruction.

The method introduces an image-conditioned generative reconstruction model based on 3D Gaussian Splats. This model uses information from multi-view 2D diffusion to construct a 3D representation. That representation then guides the diffusion model's reverse sampling process toward better agreement across views. Information therefore flows in both directions: image-generation priors inform reconstruction, and reconstructed geometry helps refine image generation.

Experiments report better performance than state-of-the-art methods and realistic avatars with high fidelity in geometry and appearance from a single image. Ablations support both conditioning reconstruction on multi-view priors and refining the sampling trajectory through explicit 3D information. These findings support the paper's central idea that closely coupling the two models can make their complementary information more useful.
neurips-2024-human-3diffusion-realistic-.tldr: Human-3Diffusion couples multi-view diffusion with 3D Gaussian reconstruction to create realistic single-image avatars with improved cross-view consistency.

paragraphs: Unsupervised visible-infrared person re-identification matches people across ordinary and infrared images without annotations. Existing cluster-based approaches often represent a person using a cluster center. The paper argues that this emphasizes what the examples share while overlooking their differences and the range of appearances within a cluster.

The proposed method adds two kinds of prototypes to contrastive learning. A hard prototype is the sample farthest from the cluster center, making divergent examples more prominent in the learning objective. A dynamic prototype is selected randomly from within the cluster, encouraging the model to account for varied examples instead of repeatedly aligning images with one fixed representative.

A progressive training strategy gradually shifts attention toward divergence and variety to avoid deteriorating the clusters. This scheduling connects the richer prototypes to the stability of the unsupervised learning process. Experiments on SYSU-MM01 and RegDB validate the method's effectiveness. The results support representing a cluster through more than its center, while introducing those additional learning signals gradually.
neurips-2024-learning-commonality-diverg.tldr: The method progressively adds hard and randomly selected cluster prototypes to improve unsupervised person matching across visible and infrared images.

paragraphs: Conformal prediction produces sets of possible answers to express uncertainty. Two properties matter together: the sets should provide appropriate coverage for the relevant populations, and they should be small enough to remain informative. The paper develops Conformal Prediction with Length-Optimization, or CPL, to address these objectives within one framework.

CPL constructs prediction sets with optimal or near-optimal length while ensuring conditional validity under various classes of covariate shifts. The framework includes marginal coverage and group-conditional coverage as key cases. Its theoretical results distinguish sample regimes: with infinitely many samples, strong duality establishes conditional validity and length optimality; with finite samples, the authors establish conditional validity.

Experiments compare CPL with state-of-the-art methods on real and synthetic data, covering classification, regression, and language-model-based multiple-choice answering. The authors report better prediction-set sizes across these evaluations. The contribution is a principled connection between coverage requirements and set-size optimization, with theoretical guarantees stated separately for infinite and finite data and empirical evidence about the resulting efficiency.
neurips-2024-length-optimization-in-conf.tldr: CPL jointly addresses prediction-set size and coverage, with conditional-validity guarantees and length-optimality results in the infinite-sample regime.

paragraphs: A 3D object's realism depends on its material properties as well as its visible colors. Materials determine how its appearance responds to lighting, yet existing assets and generative models often lack authentic material information. Make-it-Real addresses the time-consuming task of assigning suitable materials manually by using a multimodal language model to support that process.

The approach first uses GPT-4V's ability to recognize and describe materials to construct a detailed material library. It then combines visual evidence with hierarchical text prompts to match materials to the appropriate components of a 3D object. This links the model's interpretation of an object's parts to references that can guide material creation.

The matched materials serve as references for generating spatially varying reflectance properties, using the object's original albedo map. The authors report that this process substantially improves visual authenticity and can fit into a 3D content-creation workflow. The contribution connects material understanding, component-level matching, and material generation into a pipeline intended to reduce the burden of producing realistically surfaced 3D assets.
neurips-2024-make-it-real-unleashing-lar.tldr: Make-it-Real uses GPT-4V to identify and match materials to 3D object parts, guiding the generation of more realistic surface properties.

paragraphs: MVInpainter treats 3D editing as coordinated inpainting across multiple 2D views. Instead of generating each view in full, it edits selected regions with guidance from a reference. The unmasked parts of the images provide clues about the scene, reducing the generation problem and allowing the method to operate without explicit camera-pose conditions.

To keep edited views consistent, the method combines video-derived motion priors with reference-based appearance guidance through attention. It also uses slot attention to aggregate high-level optical-flow features from unmasked regions. These features provide information for controlling camera movement, enabling both training and inference without supplied poses. The design uses the visible scene as a source of motion and appearance constraints.

Experiments on object-centric and forward-facing scene datasets demonstrate applications including object removal, synthesis, insertion, and replacement across views. The findings support multi-view inpainting as a bridge between 2D image editing and 3D scene editing. Its central advantage is making use of existing image content and shared reference guidance to coordinate edits in challenging scenes.
neurips-2024-mvinpainter-learning-multi-.tldr: MVInpainter coordinates reference-guided edits across multiple images, using unmasked scene information to support consistent 3D editing without explicit camera poses.

paragraphs: Conventional semi-supervised learning assumes that every class has at least some labeled examples. Open-world semi-supervised learning relaxes that assumption: the unlabeled data can contain classes absent from the labeled set. A method that treats every unlabeled example as belonging to a familiar class can consequently misclassify unfamiliar examples and reduce overall accuracy.

OwMatch adapts self-labeling and consistency methods to this setting. Its framework combines conditional self-labeling with open-world hierarchical thresholding. These components address the assignment and use of labels when the unlabeled pool includes both known and unknown classes. The paper also analyzes how class distributions can be estimated from the unlabeled data.

The statistical analysis establishes an unbiasedness result for the label-assignment estimator. This is a claim about the estimator, rather than a claim that every assigned label is correct. Empirical evaluations show substantial improvements over previous methods for both known and unknown classes. The findings support explicitly accommodating unfamiliar classes in the learning procedure instead of relying on the conventional shared-class assumption.
neurips-2024-owmatch-conditional-self-la.tldr: OwMatch adapts self-labeling and consistency to unlabeled data containing unseen classes, improving results for both known and unknown categories.

paragraphs: PaCE addresses a tension in language-model alignment: suppressing undesirable content can also remove useful information and weaken language capabilities. Some existing approaches additionally require expensive fine-tuning for each alignment task. The paper instead proposes editing internal activations during inference using a representation organized around semantic concepts.

The method constructs a large dictionary in activation space, with each dictionary element corresponding to a concept. For a particular alignment task, a concept partitioner labels the concepts as benign or undesirable. Sparse coding then expresses the model's activations as combinations of these dictionary elements. Removing the undesirable components changes the internal representation in a direction intended to support the task's alignment goal.

Experiments cover response detoxification, improved faithfulness, and sentiment revision. The authors report state-of-the-art alignment performance while maintaining linguistic capabilities. The stated findings support selective concept removal as a way to change model behavior without discarding as much benign content. The task-specific partition is central: it determines which parts of the shared concept representation the intervention removes.
neurips-2024-pace-parsimonious-concept-e.tldr: PaCE decomposes language-model activations into semantic concepts and removes task-specific undesirable components while preserving linguistic capabilities in its evaluations.

paragraphs: A summary can be well written and broadly useful without emphasizing what a particular reader cares about. PersonalSum investigates this difference between generic summarization and individual preferences. The paper identifies a shortage of datasets based on the public's own summary choices, rather than preferences inferred from generic datasets or imposed through hypothetical tasks.

The authors introduce a manually annotated dataset containing user profiles, personalized summaries, and the article sentences supporting those summaries. It also includes machine-generated generic summaries and their source sentences. This structure supports examining how readers' selections differ from generic model outputs while retaining a connection between each summary and the original article.

The paper studies entities and topics, plot, and article structure as possible signals for personalization in a few-shot in-context learning setting. Preliminary findings suggest that entities and topics explain only part of the variation in user preferences. Personalized summarization remains challenging for the evaluated language models. The dataset therefore supports studying personalization as a richer problem than simply choosing which named entities or topics a summary should mention.
neurips-2024-personalsum-a-user-subjecti.tldr: PersonalSum provides human-authored personalized summaries and finds that reader preferences extend beyond topic selection, remaining challenging for existing language models.

paragraphs: Neural Episodic Control uses a differentiable dictionary to store memories for reinforcement learning. Although inspired by episodic memory, it previously lacked a direct theoretical connection to associative-memory models. This paper establishes that its dictionary fits within the Universal Hopfield Network framework, linking a useful control mechanism to a mathematical framework for memory.

The authors introduce a continuous approximation to the dictionary's readout operation. This allows them to derive two energy functions that are Lyapunov functions for the dynamics, giving a formal way to characterize the resulting memory process. The approximation is the bridge that makes this dynamical analysis possible.

Empirically, the dictionary outperforms the Max separation function, which had previously been argued to be optimal. Replacing its Euclidean-distance kernel with a Manhattan-distance kernel improves performance further. The authors attribute these results to the dictionary's capacity to generalize and introduce an evaluation criterion that separates generalization from memorization. This distinction matters because retrieving stored information and extending beyond it can contribute differently to measured associative-memory performance.
neurips-2024-relating-hopfield-networks-.tldr: The paper connects episodic-control dictionaries to Hopfield networks and shows why separating memorization from generalization matters when evaluating associative memory.

paragraphs: Inverse optimization learns an expert's unknown objective from records of their decisions. The paper expands the class of objectives this framework can represent by placing them in a reproducing kernel Hilbert space. This provides an infinite-dimensional feature representation, allowing the learned objective to be expressed in a richer hypothesis class.

An infinite-dimensional formulation could appear difficult to train directly. For a specific training loss, the authors prove a variant of the representer theorem that turns the learning problem into a finite-dimensional convex optimization program. This result links the expressive kernel formulation to a concrete optimization problem without requiring an explicit infinite list of features.

The paper then addresses the computational scaling associated with kernel methods through Sequential Selection Optimization, an algorithm for training the proposed Kernel Inverse Optimization model efficiently. Learning-from-demonstration tasks on the MuJoCo benchmark validate the model's generalization capabilities and the algorithm's effectiveness. The contribution combines a richer representation of expert objectives, a tractable reformulation for the chosen loss, and a training method aimed at scalability.
neurips-2024-scalable-kernel-inverse-opt.tldr: Kernel Inverse Optimization learns richer expert objectives through a finite convex reformulation and a training algorithm designed to improve scalability.

paragraphs: Instruction fine-tuning adapts pretrained language models using examples of desired behavior. The paper starts from evidence that small, high-quality datasets can perform well, suggesting that larger collections contain redundant or even harmful examples. The practical problem is identifying which data to retain without relying on labor-intensive human curation.

SHED is an automated refinement framework based on Shapley value. It selects data for instruction fine-tuning without human intervention or commercial language models. The authors also examine whether the resulting datasets remain useful across different language models. This transferability matters because a selected dataset becomes more broadly useful if its value is not confined to one particular model.

Extensive experiments across tasks and language models show that SHED outperforms state-of-the-art selection methods. In particular, selected datasets containing only 10% of the original examples achieve performance comparable to or better than training on the full datasets. The reported results support automated data refinement as a way to retain training value while substantially reducing the amount of instruction data used.
neurips-2024-shed-shapley-based-automate.tldr: SHED automatically selects transferable instruction-tuning datasets, with 10% subsets matching or exceeding full-dataset performance in the reported experiments.

paragraphs: Federated optimization must balance communication between participants with computation performed locally. DANE achieves strong communication efficiency by exploiting similarities in the second-order structure of local objectives, but requires accurate solutions to local subproblems. The paper develops S-DANE to retain this communication advantage while easing the computational burden of those local solves.

S-DANE introduces an auxiliary sequence of proximal centers and relaxes the accuracy condition for the local subproblems. It preserves DANE's deterministic communication complexity while improving local computation efficiency. The method also supports partial client participation and arbitrary stochastic local solvers, extending the choices available for carrying out the local work.

An accelerated version achieves the best-known communication complexity among existing methods for distributed convex optimization while retaining favorable local computation efficiency. The authors also develop adaptive versions using line search. These have provable efficiency and can exploit local second-order similarity without prior knowledge of parameters. The contribution addresses communication, local solution accuracy, and parameter adaptation within a related family of optimization methods.
neurips-2024-stabilized-proximal-point-m.tldr: S-DANE preserves strong communication guarantees while allowing cheaper local solves, with accelerated and adaptive variants for distributed convex optimization.

paragraphs: The paper studies optimization when an algorithm can query noisy function values but cannot directly access derivatives. Its setting assumes strong convexity and second-order smoothness, with the title specifying a Lipschitz Hessian. The main question is how accurately an algorithm can identify a good solution from this restricted, noisy feedback.

The authors give matching upper and lower bounds for the minimax simple-regret rate. The upper bound describes performance an algorithm can achieve, while the lower bound establishes the corresponding worst-case difficulty. Their agreement provides a tight characterization of the rate within the stated problem setting. The proposed algorithm combines an initial bootstrapping stage with a mirror-descent stage.

A key technical result sharply characterizes a gradient estimator based on spherical sampling under higher-order smoothness. This lets the algorithm balance estimation bias against variance optimally for the analysis. A new iterative bootstrapping method also maintains performance when the Hessian is unbounded. The contribution therefore combines a characterization of fundamental sample requirements with an algorithm designed to attain them.
neurips-2024-stochastic-zeroth-order-opt.tldr: The paper establishes matching minimax regret bounds and an attaining algorithm for strongly convex, second-order-smooth optimization using only noisy function evaluations.

paragraphs: Logic synthesis constructs an optimized circuit that implements a specified function. The paper investigates why differentiable neural architecture search struggles with this task, finding problems with exact functionality, scaling, and sensitivity to hyperparameters. Its empirical analysis identifies excessive skip connections, a mismatch between network and circuit structure, and uneven learning difficulty across input-output examples.

The authors use these findings to design a regularized, triangle-shaped circuit-generation network. Its structure addresses the identified search problems with the goal of producing accurate circuits at larger scales. They then optimize the generated circuits using an evolutionary algorithm assisted by a reinforcement-learning-agent restarting technique, connecting circuit construction with a subsequent optimization stage.

Experiments on four circuit benchmarks demonstrate precise generation of circuits containing up to 1,200 nodes. The synthesized circuits also significantly outperform state-of-the-art results from several competitive winners of the IWLS 2022 and 2023 competitions. These findings support tailoring neural search to circuit structure and learning behavior, with exact generation demonstrated at the reported scale.
neurips-2024-towards-next-generation-log.tldr: A circuit-specific neural generation framework addresses architecture-search failures and precisely generates circuits with up to 1,200 nodes in the reported experiments.

paragraphs: The paper addresses unauthorized training on 3D point-cloud data that may contain sensitive information. It proposes a framework that makes the distributed data unlearnable while also providing a restoration procedure for authorized use. This second part addresses a practical difficulty: protection is less useful if it also prevents intended users from learning from the data.

The protection scheme uses class-wise settings established through a category-adaptive allocation strategy, with multiple transformations assigned to samples. Restoration applies inverse matrix transformations at the class level. The two procedures are designed together so that transforming the data for protection is paired with a way to recover its usefulness for authorized training.

The authors support the framework with both theoretical analysis and empirical evaluation across six datasets, sixteen models, and two tasks. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed protection-and-restoration approach in the studied settings. The central contribution is treating controlled recovery as part of unlearnable-data design, alongside the goal of obstructing unauthorized learning from 3D point clouds.
neurips-2024-unlearnable-3d-point-clouds.tldr: The framework protects 3D point clouds through class-wise transformations and restores their training usefulness through corresponding inverse transformations.

paragraphs: Traditional federated learning updates every parameter of each local model and averages those parameters after each training round. The paper argues that this can repeatedly disrupt cooperation between layers in the global model. It calls the problem layer mismatch and connects it to slower convergence and reduced performance on client tasks.

FedPart changes the update process by training only one layer or a few layers during each communication round. To keep learning and sharing effective across the network, it includes strategies for choosing which layers are trainable, including sequential updates and training cycles spanning multiple rounds. The selection schedule is therefore part of how partial updates support the overall model.

Theoretical analysis and experiments show that FedPart improves convergence speed and accuracy compared with conventional full-network update strategies, while reducing communication and computation overhead. The findings support coordinating which layers change in each round as a way to improve federated training. The reported benefit goes beyond reducing work per round: it also addresses the disruption caused by repeated parameter averaging.
neurips-2024-why-go-full-elevating-feder.tldr: FedPart updates selected layers each federated round to reduce layer mismatch, improving convergence and accuracy while lowering computation and communication costs.
